The pacing of the story feels very natural, appropriate, and balanced. For the majority of the narrative, "story time" aligns closely with "real-world time," matching the slow, steady, and routine rhythm of a short river crossing on a cable ferry. The brief moments of quiet observation and sparse dialogue mirror the actual few minutes it takes to cross the river in the fog. 

At the very end, the author employs a subtle stretching of time when Ilse's phone rings. Drawing out the few seconds it takes for the phone to vibrate, for her to look at the screen, hover her thumb over the green button, and listen to two rings creates a moment of quiet internal tension before she puts it away and returns to the steady rhythm of her work.
